title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for short-stay turnover
audience: Owners of short-stay turnover businesses, including solo cleaners, who reset holiday rentals and serviced apartments between guests for hosts and managers.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer for a turnover
instruction.body: 'I clean between guests' is a service. 'I reset the unit to your checklist within the window we agree, send photos before check-in, and return before the next check-in to fix any listed item that was missed, for one fixed price per turnover' is an offer. The host buys a unit that is ready for the next guest, and certainty that the checklist has been done. Do not promise guest outcomes, such as reviews or ratings.

instruction.heading: The five parts of a turnover offer
instruction.body: Set the outcome (a unit reset to a named checklist), the time frame (a turnover window agreed with the host and measured on past turnovers), what the host must provide (checkout time, linen and consumables, access codes, a list of what guests leave), the certainty you give (checklist, photos, a cleaning log) and the risk you carry (a return visit before the next check-in). Put the scope, window and exclusions in writing, because a written quote becomes binding once accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Packages for turnovers
instruction.body: A good-better-best layout suits turnovers: a standard turnover to the checklist, a deep turnover with extra listed tasks, and a block price for a booked calendar. Beyond Pricing shows separate bands for general and deep turnovers, and suggests fixed rates suit small to medium properties while hourly rates suit larger or luxury homes (vendor source, 28 October 2026). Jobber shows stepped packages as a general method (published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024).

instruction.heading: One total per turnover, and the levy question
instruction.body: Show one total per turnover and say whether GST is included (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024; WA guidance for WA). Victoria's short-stay levy is a separate matter. The State Revenue Office says booking platforms, and owners or tenants who accept bookings directly, must register for stays under 28 consecutive days from 1 January 2025. The page does not state the rate. Check with the host who pays the levy in your arrangement, and show it as its own line if it applies to your price.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and the fix-first visit
instruction.body: Offer a return visit before the next check-in for any listed item that was missed. Under the consumer guarantees, a business must be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (Consumer Victoria's guidance, 13 October 2023; a Victorian page, so check your state's consumer agency). That page sets no fix window, so set and test your own. A 'no refunds' line does not override service rights (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025).

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence that a host would repeat: the unit is ready for the next guest by the check-in time.
Agree the turnover window and checkout time with the host, and measure your past turnovers against it.
List what the host must supply and what guests leave, and write both into the offer.
Add one certainty element: a checklist and photos sent before check-in.
Set the fix window and check that your calendar can hold the return visit.
Price from measured time and cost, compare with the per-turnover band, and state which one you used.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A solo cleaner turns over a two-bedroom Melbourne apartment three times a week for one host. The host says other cleaners charge less per turnover and asks for a lower fixed price on the same scope.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the offer contain, and how should the cleaner answer the request for a lower price?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cleaner offers a fixed price per turnover for a checklist reset, with photos before check-in and a return visit before the next check-in for any listed item that was missed. The vendor band for a general two-bedroom turnover is $90 to $130 (Beyond Pricing, 28 October 2026), and the same source uses $120 as an illustration. The cleaner states that the price covers the checklist, the photos and the return visit, and does not compete on the lowest figure in the band. If the host wants a lower price, the cleaner shows which tasks or time the host is asking to remove and prices that change, rather than cutting the price on the same scope. The cleaner also asks whether the host has registered for the Victorian short-stay levy, because owners or tenants who accept bookings directly must register (SRO Victoria, 4 March 2025).

commonErrors.error: Pricing per turnover without a checklist or a turnover window.
commonErrors.prevention: Put both in the written offer, so the host can see what the price buys.

commonErrors.error: Promising guest outcomes, such as ratings or reviews.
commonErrors.prevention: Promise the clean, the photos and the return visit, and nothing you do not control.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the host pays the levy, or that the cleaner does.
commonErrors.prevention: Check who registers and who pays. The research did not state the levy rate.

commonErrors.error: Relying on one city's labour benchmark.
commonErrors.prevention: Benchmarks differ by city in the vendor data. Use your own hours and cost.
Check your council's registration rule. The research checked council rules only in outline.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Victoria only: booking platforms, and owners or tenants who accept bookings directly, must register for the short-stay levy for stays under 28 consecutive days from 1 January 2025 (State Revenue Office Victoria, 4 March 2025). Other states' rules were not checked.
Price display: show the total including GST (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024). Consumer guarantees for services cannot be removed by contract (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025).
Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence or authority. Licence and insurance rules for turnover cleaning were not researched, so check the rules for the state where you work.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: Price a turnover to a checklist and a turnover window, with a return visit before the next check-in.
Check who registers for and pays any levy, and whether your council requires registration.
Gaps: no government or trade-body turnover price, levy rate or council rule was found in the research.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a turnover offer does the host buy?
options: Your hourly rate on its own
A unit reset to the checklist, ready for the next guest by the agreed time

knowledgeChecks.question: A host asks for a lower fixed price per turnover on the same checklist. What is the best response?
options: Cut the price without changing the scope
Show which tasks or time the host is asking you to remove, and price that change
Agree, and skip the checklist photos

knowledgeChecks.question: According to the research, who must register for the Victorian short-stay levy?
options: Booking platforms, and owners or tenants who accept bookings directly
Nobody, because it is a federal scheme

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted; a quote should recover cost plus a margin.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Ask us: Estimates and quotes', https://consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/publications/ask-us-estimates-and-quotes, last updated 18 November 2024. Western Australia only. Supports: a quote is a fixed price and an estimate can move; extra work needs the customer's permission; a written quote should state the job, possible extra costs, materials, labour and time to finish.
business.gov.au, 'Display prices', https://business.gov.au/legal/fair-trading/display-prices, page metadata 18 January 2024. Supports: displayed prices should show the total price, including GST.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Victoria. Supports: a business should be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge; the page sets no fix-window length.

Beyond Pricing, 'Short-term rental cleaning fees (Australia)', https://beyondpricing.com/au/blog/how-much-should-you-charge-for-cleaning-fees-in-your-australian-holiday-rental, dated 28 October 2026. Vendor source; short-stay fee data. Supports: per-turnover bands by property size; move-in and move-out bands by bedroom count; a $120 per-turnover illustration; city labour benchmarks; fixed rates suit smaller properties and hourly rates suit larger or luxury homes.

State Revenue Office Victoria, 'Register now for the short-stay levy', https://sro.vic.gov.au/news/register-now-short-stay-levy, published 4 March 2025. Victoria. Supports: the levy applies to stays under 28 consecutive days from 1 January 2025; booking platforms and owners or tenants who accept bookings directly must register. The page does not state the rate.

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, page last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading statements about prices are prohibited.

business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', https://www.business.gov.au/Products-and-services/Fair-trading/Warranties-and-refunds, last updated 27 May 2025. Supports: an optional warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees; a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services.

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Older source, updated after 2022. Supports: stepped packages where each higher level adds something the customer can see; house cleaning is one trade example.

Notes: $120 is an illustration in the vendor source. The band figures are a vendor source. The levy rate was not stated on the SRO page. The council example (City of Port Phillip) was not checked in detail and is not cited as a rule.
